To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. The total cluster masses derived from our AMI SZ data are typically lower than those derived from X-ray data, but in better agreement with weak lensing masses.

(i) The AMI cluster analysis method yields consistent cluster parameters, (ii) AMI and WL cluster parameters agree, (iii) Suzaku/Chanda X-ray masses are higher than AMI masses, (iv) AMI and X-ray temperatures differ, (v) AMI data are less sensitive than X-ray data to ICM disturbance, and (vi) AMI data indicate that mergers affect the ICM out to large r.
(i) The SZ and WL estimates of M_T(r500) agree well, while the X-ray estimates tend to be higher.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of the ICM in galaxy clusters.
the use of the SZ effect to study the structure and evolution of clusters of galaxies and the properties of their ICM.
the study of clusters of galaxies
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the AMI SZ data are consistent with X-ray and WL data but that, for the clusters studied, the AMI data suggest that the higher X-ray mass estimates are likely to be due to a combination of the effects of mergers on the X-ray signal and of the use of T_X values that are significantly higher than T_AMI.

the AMI data, combined with the WL data, show that the clusters in this sample have a mean mass M_T(r500) = 1.1x10^15 M_Sun and that there is no evidence for any significant bias in the mass estimates.

, in the outer regions, the SZ data are consistent with X-ray and weak-lensing data and that the X-ray data are consistent with the weak-lensing data, but that the X-ray masses are higher, particularly for the stronger merger clusters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, at large radius, the SZ is a better indicator of the total mass and the X-ray is a better indicator for the gas mass.
the AMI data are consistent with a picture in which the X-ray mass is overestimated for strong mergers, and the WL mass underestimated.
the AMI SZ data are in good agreement with X-ray and weak-lensing estimates of cluster mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that

SZ observations can be used to obtain cluster parameters out to r200, with good agreement with WL and X-ray estimates, and that the use of SZ data to obtain T_AMI can be used to constrain X-ray temperatures, and thereby cluster masses, in mergers.
AMI SZ data are a valuable addition to X-ray and WL studies of cluster masses.
AMI SZ observations can provide accurate estimates of cluster parameters, including the virial mass and temperature, out to the virialized region.
